judged_text: The new token fetch runs unconditionally on every connection creation — no expiry check, no APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED gate, and no timeout — replacing jsforce's lazy refresh-on-401 with a per-operation round trip plus credential write. Every Salesforce calendar operation now costs an extra outbound token request and a DB write even when the stored token is still valid, adding latency and avoidable rate-limit exposure on login.salesforce.com, and a refresh-endpoint hiccup now fails operations that previously would have succeeded on the still-valid stored token.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code now performs a refresh-token POST to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and then `prisma.credential.update(...)` *before* returning the `jsforce.Connection` (lines added around the `fetch(...)`, `await response.json()`, and DB update). There is no expiry/validity check on the stored token prior to refreshing, no use of the new `refreshOAuthTokens` helper / `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` gating in this path, and the `fetch` has no explicit timeout/abort handling. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/reliability concern (extra outbound call + DB write and new failure point) even if it may be an intentional design change rather than a strict correctness bug.
